messages:
kim_support: FYI cust-8273 just opened an escalation — their embeddings indexer started failing after we pinned a model. They say embeddings length is now 384 but their index expects 512.

ajay_ml: Can you paste a sample request/response?

kim_support: Repro from customer (redacted key):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"embed-open-512-pinned","input":"hello"}'
```
Response body snippet: `{"model":"embed-open-512-pinned","embedding":[..., /* 384 floats */]}` -> length 384.

rachel_infra: Quick thought — "pinned" aliases can still point to a variant. Have we confirmed the alias mapping for this account? Sometimes an alias get remapped to a quantized/384 variant during a routing change.

ajay_ml: I ran a quick trace for that request id (redacted) in the serving logs:
```
2024-07-12T15:03:21Z request=.... model_alias=embed-open-512 routing_decision=variant(embed-open-384-q8) reason=alias_mapping
```
Looks like routing selected `embed-open-384-q8`.

jonas_custsuccess: If the alias is pointed incorrectly we should either revert alias for that org or force-route their traffic to the previous exact version. Customer wants a hotfix asap — indexer is failing nightly batch jobs.

kim_support: opened internal ticket INF-1294 with model-onboarding. For mitigation I added a tenant-level override to force `embed-open-512@2024-05-10` for cust-8273.

rachel_infra: I also checked infra autoscaler around the incident window — there was a transient memory pressure event which triggered a quick fallback mapping for several aliases to smaller variants. That explains why some pinned aliases ended up at 384.

ajay_ml: Action items I ran locally to reproduce:
1) call embeddings with `model: "embed-open-512-pinned"` -> got 384
2) call with explicit version `model: "embed-open-512@2024-05-10"` -> got 512
3) check alias mapping API: `GET /internal/model-aliases/embed-open-512` -> returned `"target":"embed-open-384-q8"`

kim_support: Customer accepted the tenant override and indexer resumed. They're asking for permanent fix & root-cause.

rachel_infra: Root cause hypothesis: alias metadata doesn't include vector-dim guard, so runtime can remap alias -> lower-dim variant during fallback. We should enforce `vec_dim` compatibility at routing time.

jonas_custsuccess: Recommend we: (a) update alias mappings to include `vec_dim` and reject remap if dims mismatch, (b) add regression test/eval that detects vec-len changes for pinned aliases, (c) notify impacted customers + offer one week of credit.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment completed: model-alias-safe-guard v2024-07-12 ✅

ajay_ml: Longer term we should also emit an explicit warning in the API when returned embedding length != model catalog declared vec_len (for easier detection by customers).

kim_support: Filed follow-up RFC to add vec-dim validation into routing + add CI eval. Ticket INF-1294 -> linked to ONB-58. Customer notif drafted; handing to CS to send.

jonas_custsuccess: I'll send the notification and the credit offer. Good catch. :thumbsup:

kim_support: TL;DR: customer saw 384 after pin because alias remapped to a 384 quantized variant during a fallback; tenant override restored expected 512; next steps: enforce vec-dim checks on alias/route, add regression tests, and notify/customer remediation.
